question.worked_solution:
First, we isolate the absolute value on the left side of the equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}7|2x-5|+1 & =15 \\ 7|2x-5| & =14 \\ |2x-5| & =2\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we have the following two cases:

- If $|2x-5|=2x-5,$ we obtain:

$$
\begin{aligned}|2x-5| & =2 \\ 2x-5 & =2 \\ 2x & =7 \\ x & =\frac{7}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

- If $|2x-5|=-(2x-5),$ we obtain:

$$
\begin{aligned}|2x-5| & =2 \\ -(2x-5) & =2 \\ -2x+5 & =2 \\ -2x & =-3 \\ x & =\frac{3}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solutions are $x=\frac{3}{2}$ and $x=\frac{7}{2}.$
